# Final Review Proposal
**Producer:** agent:claude/claude-opus-4-6

## Summary

Reviewed the full changeset for tanksim-6e5.4.7 (nitrification alkalinity depletion validation). The core implementation is correct: alkalinity is deducted exactly once per mg N at the TAN-oxidation step (AOB + comammox), NOB does not double-charge, named constants match literature stoichiometry (2/14.007 meq/mg N for nitrification, 1/14.007 for denitrification), and the denitrification return path is cleanly prepared via the `alkalinity_produced_meq` output field. Budget and tracing integration correctly surfaces alkalinity deltas. All 6 new tests pass and cover the acceptance criteria comprehensively. The pre-existing `save_load_with_active_cycle_state` test failure is confirmed unrelated. Two minor issues found: (1) `alk_budget` shadow variable is not updated after comammox, creating asymmetry with the DO budget pattern; (2) `BudgetMetric` allocations occur even when diagnostics are disabled.

## Amendments

1. In nitrogen_cycle.rs, after the comammox step (around line 350), `alk_budget` is not decremented by `comammox_alk_cost`, while `do_budget` IS always decremented after each step. Since nothing reads `alk_budget` after comammox this is harmless today, but if a future step (e.g. denitrification) needs the running alkalinity budget for rate-limiting, the stale value would silently over-allocate. Add `alk_budget = (alk_budget - comammox_alk_cost).max(0.0);` after line 350 to match the DO budget pattern and prevent a latent accounting bug.
   Rationale: Asymmetry between DO and alkalinity budget tracking creates a maintenance trap. The DO pattern (always update the running budget after each consumer) is the safe default; skipping the update for alkalinity only because 'nothing reads it later' is fragile when E4b denitrification will add a new alkalinity-producing step that may need the running budget for sanity checks or rate-limiting.
2. In engine.rs, `StageTrace::metric()` unconditionally allocates `BudgetMetric` (including a heap `String` for the label) even when neither budget tracking nor tracing is enabled. For the nitrogen_cycle stage alone this is 5 allocations per tick, silently dropped if no budget ledger exists. Guard the allocation: either check `ctx.budget.is_some()` before calling `metric()`, or make `metric()` a no-op when a `budget_active` flag is false — similar to how `note()` already guards on `self.enabled`.
   Rationale: In long simulations without diagnostics (the common production path), this creates thousands of unnecessary heap allocations per simulated hour across all stages. The fix is trivial (one boolean guard) and follows the existing pattern used for notes.
